articles.title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Starship emerged from the clouds after surviving the extreme heat of re-entering Earth’s atmosphere, then descended slowly over SpaceX’s south Texas Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday (November 14, 2026) pulled off the first-ever “catch” of a spaceship, a technical feat showing the feasibility of fully reusable rockets that would bring affordable spaceflight one step closer to reality. The Starship emerged from the clouds after surviving the extreme heat of re-entering Earth’s atmosphere, then descended slowly over SpaceX’s south Texas Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2. The success marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems -- a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible. “That was the Holy Grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds outside Starbase broke into ecstatic cheers as the spaceship came into view, with the 1977 soft rock hit “Baby Come Back” serving as the soundtrack of the nerve-wracking final descent on SpaceX’s official livestream. “I really do believe this is the dawn of the space age,” said Dane Walter, 38, a spectator who came from Corpus Christi, Texas. “And truly, I consider it an equivalent moment to the Wright brothers at Kitty Hawk.” It was the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. Up until now, spaceships have been single-use items, discarded or destroyed after missions, making each launch an expensive resource-intensive venture. The Starship spacecraft that gives SpaceX’s rocket system its name orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Musk’s Starlink internet constellation during its 22-hour journey. SpaceX had previously captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was more complex because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude compared to boosters.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “I hugged ship 42 upon its return,” Mr. Musk posted on X about the captured vessel, sharing videos taken from various angles and saying it “looks great!”

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #27 of 30 (15 NOV)

📰 SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’

📌 Published: 15 Nov 2026, 12:54:53 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Starship emerged from the clouds after surviving the extreme heat of re-entering Earth’s atmosphere, then descended slowly over SpaceX’s south Texas Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday (November 14, 2026) pulled off the first-ever “catch” of a spaceship, a technical feat showing the feasibility of fully reusable rockets that would bring affordable spaceflight one step closer to reality. The Starship emerged from the clouds after surviving the extreme heat of re-entering Earth’s atmosphere, then descended slowly over SpaceX’s south Texas Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2. The success marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems -- a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible. “That was the Holy Grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds outside Starbase broke into ecstatic cheers as the spaceship came into view, with the 1977 soft rock hit “Baby Come Back” serving as the soundtrack of the nerve-wracking final descent on SpaceX’s official livestream. “I really do believe this is the dawn of the space age,” said Dane Walter, 38, a spectator who came from Corpus Christi, Texas. “And truly, I consider it an equivalent moment to the Wright brothers at Kitty Hawk.” It was the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. Up until now, spaceships have been single-use items, discarded or destroyed after missions, making each launch an expensive resource-intensive venture. The Starship spacecraft that gives SpaceX’s rocket system its name orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Musk’s Starlink internet constellation during its 22-hour journey. SpaceX had previously captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was more complex because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude compared to boosters.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “I hugged ship 42 upon its return,” Mr. Musk posted on X about the captured vessel, sharing videos taken from various angles and saying it “looks great!”

articles.title: Diabetes linked with 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's, review finds
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People with diabetes could be at a 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's disease, compared to those living without the metabolic disorder, a review of studies has found. Researchers, led by those from Australia's Curtin University, conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 40 studies. They found that if 1,000 people living with type 2 diabetes were followed for a year, an estimaated average of 4.7 would develop Alzheimer's disease, a neurodegenerative disorder in which memory and thought processes steadily decline with age. Cognitive risk prevention should be integrated into diabetes care, they said. "Individuals with T2D (type 2 diabetes) experienced approximately five AD (Alzheimer's disease) cases per 1,000 person-years and a 53 per cent higher risk of AD, supporting the rationale for integrating cognitive risk prevention into diabetes care," the authors wrote in the study published in the journal Alzheimer's Research and Therapy. Study author Emmanuel Adewuyi, an investigator fellow at Curtin University's school of population health, said the review was important as it quantifies the relative risk and incidence of Alzheimer's in people living with type 2 diabetes. "While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred," Adewuyi said. "Relative risk tells us how two groups compare, while incidence tells us how often new cases occur: putting those numbers together gives us a clearer picture of the burden of Alzheimer's disease among people living with type 2 diabetes," the author said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Databases including MEDLINE, CINAHL and Embase were searched from for publications since inception until April 2026. Forty studies, involving 27,102,559 data points, and looking at the incidence of Alzheimer's disease among people with diabetes or link between the two disorders were analysed.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (15 NOV)

📰 Diabetes linked with 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's, review finds

📌 Published: 15 Nov 2026, 12:39:39 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People with diabetes could be at a 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's disease, compared to those living without the metabolic disorder, a review of studies has found. Researchers, led by those from Australia's Curtin University, conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 40 studies. They found that if 1,000 people living with type 2 diabetes were followed for a year, an estimaated average of 4.7 would develop Alzheimer's disease, a neurodegenerative disorder in which memory and thought processes steadily decline with age. Cognitive risk prevention should be integrated into diabetes care, they said. "Individuals with T2D (type 2 diabetes) experienced approximately five AD (Alzheimer's disease) cases per 1,000 person-years and a 53 per cent higher risk of AD, supporting the rationale for integrating cognitive risk prevention into diabetes care," the authors wrote in the study published in the journal Alzheimer's Research and Therapy. Study author Emmanuel Adewuyi, an investigator fellow at Curtin University's school of population health, said the review was important as it quantifies the relative risk and incidence of Alzheimer's in people living with type 2 diabetes. "While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred," Adewuyi said. "Relative risk tells us how two groups compare, while incidence tells us how often new cases occur: putting those numbers together gives us a clearer picture of the burden of Alzheimer's disease among people living with type 2 diabetes," the author said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Databases including MEDLINE, CINAHL and Embase were searched from for publications since inception until April 2026. Forty studies, involving 27,102,559 data points, and looking at the incidence of Alzheimer's disease among people with diabetes or link between the two disorders were analysed.

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'University' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

व्यवस्थित — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Systematic' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: 91% of studies in India in last 5 decades linked air pollution to health effects: Analysis
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An analysis of more than 180 epidemiological studies examining the health impacts of air pollution across India has found that over 91% of them reported at least one adverse health association with air pollution exposure. These studies, published between 1975 and 2025, also noted that health impacts extend beyond respiratory diseases to cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, pregnancy complications, impaired child growth, tumours, blood disorders, mental and neurocognitive disorders, among others. The analysis, released on Friday, was done by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), an independent research organisation focused on revealing the trends, causes, and health impacts, as well as the solutions, to air pollution. Notably, out of 180 studies, only 40 examined air pollution's impact on rural populations, of which 38 reported at least one adverse health association, indicating that air pollution's health impacts are not confined to urban areas. Further, most studies were conducted on Delhi (26) to examine the link between health and air pollution. The national capital was followed by Punjab with 13 studies, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh with 11 each, West Bengal with 10, Tamil Nadu with nine, Karnataka with eight and Telangana with seven, the report said. In a statement, CREA analyst Manoj Kumar said, "The findings highlight the need to move beyond a city-centric approach and explicitly include rural areas through a regional, airshed-based approach in the next phase of National Clean Air Programme (NCAP 2.0)." Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16. Among studies examining gaseous pollutants, statistically significant adverse health associations were reported for increased mortality, acute respiratory hospital and emergency visits, asthma-related hospital admissions, and impaired lung function. Beyond their direct health effects, gaseous pollutants such as SOx and NOx also contribute to secondary PM2.5 formation by undergoing atmospheric chemical reactions to form sulphate and nitrate particles, respectively.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kumar said, "Air pollution mitigation must adopt a multipollutant approach, addressing gaseous precursors that contribute to secondary PM2.5 and ground-level ozone formation. This requires emission reductions at major sources, including industries, power plants, residential cooking, and other combustion activities."

hinglishTracks.en: These studies, published between 1975 and 2025, also noted that health impacts extend beyond respiratory diseases to cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, pregnancy complications, impaired child growth, tumours, blood disorders, mental and neurocognitive disorders, among others.

articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (15 NOV)

📰 91% of studies in India in last 5 decades linked air pollution to health effects: Analysis

📌 Published: 15 Nov 2026, 11:52:52 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An analysis of more than 180 epidemiological studies examining the health impacts of air pollution across India has found that over 91% of them reported at least one adverse health association with air pollution exposure. These studies, published between 1975 and 2025, also noted that health impacts extend beyond respiratory diseases to cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, pregnancy complications, impaired child growth, tumours, blood disorders, mental and neurocognitive disorders, among others. The analysis, released on Friday, was done by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), an independent research organisation focused on revealing the trends, causes, and health impacts, as well as the solutions, to air pollution. Notably, out of 180 studies, only 40 examined air pollution's impact on rural populations, of which 38 reported at least one adverse health association, indicating that air pollution's health impacts are not confined to urban areas. Further, most studies were conducted on Delhi (26) to examine the link between health and air pollution. The national capital was followed by Punjab with 13 studies, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh with 11 each, West Bengal with 10, Tamil Nadu with nine, Karnataka with eight and Telangana with seven, the report said. In a statement, CREA analyst Manoj Kumar said, "The findings highlight the need to move beyond a city-centric approach and explicitly include rural areas through a regional, airshed-based approach in the next phase of National Clean Air Programme (NCAP 2.0)." Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16. Among studies examining gaseous pollutants, statistically significant adverse health associations were reported for increased mortality, acute respiratory hospital and emergency visits, asthma-related hospital admissions, and impaired lung function. Beyond their direct health effects, gaseous pollutants such as SOx and NOx also contribute to secondary PM2.5 formation by undergoing atmospheric chemical reactions to form sulphate and nitrate particles, respectively.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kumar said, "Air pollution mitigation must adopt a multipollutant approach, addressing gaseous precursors that contribute to secondary PM2.5 and ground-level ozone formation. This requires emission reductions at major sources, including industries, power plants, residential cooking, and other combustion activities."

Epidemiological (Adjective)
महामारी विज्ञान — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Epidemiological' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An analysis of more than 180 epidemiological studies examining the health impacts of air pollution across India has found that over 91% of them reported at least one adverse health association with air pollution exposure. These studies, published between 1975 and 2025, also noted that health impacts extend beyond respiratory diseases to cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, pregnancy complications, impaired child growth, tumours, blood disorders, mental and neurocognitive disorders, among others. The analysis, released on Friday, was done by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), an independent research organisation focused on revealing the trends, causes, and health impacts, as well as the solutions, to air pollution. Notably, out of 180 studies, only 40 examined air pollution's impact on rural populations, of which 38 reported at least one adverse health association, indicating that air pollution's health impacts are not confined to urban areas. Further, most studies were conducted on Delhi (26) to examine the link between health and air pollution. The national capital was followed by Punjab with 13 studies, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh with 11 each, West Bengal with 10, Tamil Nadu with nine, Karnataka with eight and Telangana with seven, the report said. In a statement, CREA analyst Manoj Kumar said, "The findings highlight the need to move beyond a city-centric approach and explicitly include rural areas through a regional, airshed-based approach in the next phase of National Clean Air Programme (NCAP 2.0)." Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16. Among studies examining gaseous pollutants, statistically significant adverse health associations were reported for increased mortality, acute respiratory hospital and emergency visits, asthma-related hospital admissions, and impaired lung function. Beyond their direct health effects, gaseous pollutants such as SOx and NOx also contribute to secondary PM2.5 formation by undergoing atmospheric chemical reactions to form sulphate and nitrate particles, respectively.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kumar said, "Air pollution mitigation must adopt a multipollutant approach, addressing gaseous precursors that contribute to secondary PM2.5 and ground-level ozone formation. This requires emission reductions at major sources, including industries, power plants, residential cooking, and other combustion activities."

articles.title: COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregnant women, call for targeted adaptation
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Studies show that exposure to extreme heat can affect pregnant women's health, pregnancy outcomes and the health of newborns

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Exposure to extreme heat during pregnancy can lead to severe outcomes, including preterm birth, stillbirth and congenital abnormalities in newborns, prompting experts at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) to highlight maternal health risks and call for targeted adaptation strategies. The issue comes into focus as countries at COP31 prepare to discuss progress towards the Global Goal on Adaptation, a framework to help nations develop key adaptation measures, including those needed to address the health impacts of climate change. However, translating growing recognition of climate-related health risks into action remains a challenge, particularly in the absence of adequate financial support. According to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), only about one per cent of formal climate finance under its financial mechanism is currently directed towards health. The broader issue of adaptation finance for developing nations is also expected to feature prominently in discussions in the coming days. Speaking to PTI on the sidelines of COP31, Alan Dangour, Director of Climate and Health at the Wellcome Trust, said the foundation is seeking to highlight the evidence of heat-related impacts on pregnant women through three key areas -- elevating the issues as a risk for women, developing guidelines and preparing health systems. “We have three key points: recognising that pregnant women are a particularly vulnerable group when it comes to climate-driven extreme heat, developing guidelines to help nurses, midwives and doctors respond to the challenges pregnant women face during heatwaves, and prepare health systems for a new world shaped by climate change, and identify the most vulnerable people so they are protected,” Dangour said. He said pregnant women were not always recognised as a particularly vulnerable group and stressed that health systems must specifically account for their needs and risks during heatwaves. “At the moment they are not recognised as such, and they need to be included in clinical guidelines. When it comes to data, we are keen that countries record the impacts of climate change on pregnant women and then work out how their guidelines and processes can protect them,” he said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “That evidence is important because we can see what works and what doesn’t in different parts of the world, and share that knowledge,” he said.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (15 NOV)

📰 COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregnant women, call for targeted adaptation

📌 Published: 15 Nov 2026, 11:45:28 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Studies show that exposure to extreme heat can affect pregnant women's health, pregnancy outcomes and the health of newborns

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Exposure to extreme heat during pregnancy can lead to severe outcomes, including preterm birth, stillbirth and congenital abnormalities in newborns, prompting experts at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) to highlight maternal health risks and call for targeted adaptation strategies. The issue comes into focus as countries at COP31 prepare to discuss progress towards the Global Goal on Adaptation, a framework to help nations develop key adaptation measures, including those needed to address the health impacts of climate change. However, translating growing recognition of climate-related health risks into action remains a challenge, particularly in the absence of adequate financial support. According to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), only about one per cent of formal climate finance under its financial mechanism is currently directed towards health. The broader issue of adaptation finance for developing nations is also expected to feature prominently in discussions in the coming days. Speaking to PTI on the sidelines of COP31, Alan Dangour, Director of Climate and Health at the Wellcome Trust, said the foundation is seeking to highlight the evidence of heat-related impacts on pregnant women through three key areas -- elevating the issues as a risk for women, developing guidelines and preparing health systems. “We have three key points: recognising that pregnant women are a particularly vulnerable group when it comes to climate-driven extreme heat, developing guidelines to help nurses, midwives and doctors respond to the challenges pregnant women face during heatwaves, and prepare health systems for a new world shaped by climate change, and identify the most vulnerable people so they are protected,” Dangour said. He said pregnant women were not always recognised as a particularly vulnerable group and stressed that health systems must specifically account for their needs and risks during heatwaves. “At the moment they are not recognised as such, and they need to be included in clinical guidelines. When it comes to data, we are keen that countries record the impacts of climate change on pregnant women and then work out how their guidelines and processes can protect them,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “That evidence is important because we can see what works and what doesn’t in different parts of the world, and share that knowledge,” he said.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Recognition (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Recognition' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Congenital (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Congenital' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Conference (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Conference' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregnant women, call for targeted adaptation", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Studies show that exposure to extreme heat can affect pregnant women's health, pregnancy outcomes and the health of newborns.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregna' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pre' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pre' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Studies show that exposure to extreme heat can affect pregnant women's health, pregnancy outcomes and the health of newborns." (Hinglish Arth: अध्ययनों से पता चलता है कि अत्यधिक गर्मी के संपर्क में आने से गर्भवती महिलाओं के स्वास्थ्य, गर्भावस्था के परिणाम और नवजात शिशुओं के स्वास्थ्य पर असर पड़ सकता है)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregnant women, call for targeted adaptation"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. “That evidence is important because we can see what works and what doesn’t in different parts of the world, and share that knowledge,” he said.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“That evidence is important because we can see what works and what doesn’t in different parts of the world, and share that knowledge,” he said." (Hinglish Arth: उन्होंने कहा, "वह सबूत महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि हम देख सकते हैं कि दुनिया के विभिन्न हिस्सों में क्या काम करता है और क्या नहीं, और उस ज्ञान को साझा कर सकते हैं।")

articles.title: Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture. India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: critical minerals / minerals / exports / economy, business and finance / business (general)

✍️ Editorial & Opinion Paragraph #1 of 30 (14 NOV)

📰 Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries

📌 Published: 14 Nov 2026, 01:00:35 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture. India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: critical minerals / minerals / exports / economy, business and finance / business (general)

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above ✍️ Editorial & Opinion passage on "Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batter' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion bat' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion bat' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries." A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. critical minerals / minerals / exports / economy, business and finance / business (general).
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "critical minerals / minerals / exports / economy, business and finance / business (general)." articles.title: Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-producing states prompt concerns as India sets 2047 target
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities. The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State. However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe. Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised. Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%. The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, the highest-grade variety of iron ore. The shortfall also raises questions over India’s continued dependence on imports. According to the Mines Ministry, the country imported 12.3 MT of iron ore in FY26, incurring an expenditure of ₹11,115 crore. Odisha accounted for more than 50% of India’s domestic iron ore production during FY26. Chhattisgarh contributed around 17.1%, followed by Karnataka at 16.6%. Capacity utilisation in the two states – albeit with significantly lower volumes than Odisha – stood at 62% and 80%, respectively, according to calculations based on BigMint data.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In January, the Odisha High Court directed that mining rights be mandatorily transferred to state-owned National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) to ensure “optimum utilisation of the mines” and “eradicate any burden on the government exchequer”.

hinglishTracks.en: With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — भारत की लौह अयस्क की मांग 2047 तक 772 मिलियन टन (एमटी) तक बढ़ने का अनुमान है, देश के सबसे बड़े लौह अयस्क भंडार धारक ओडिशा में खनिकों ने अभी तक अपनी मौजूदा क्षमताओं का लगभग 40% उपयोग नहीं किया है, जिससे संसाधन की बर्बादी और संभावित राजस्व हानि पर चिंता बढ़ गई है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — यह मुद्दा न्यायिक जांच के दायरे में आ गया है, इस महीने की शुरुआत में सुप्रीम कोर्ट और जनवरी में ओडिशा उच्च न्यायालय ने खनन क्षमताओं के कम उपयोग को चिह्नित किया था।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Underutilisation' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: कम उपयोग — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Underutilisation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse और Antonyms हैं: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable।

hinglishTracks.en: The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — ओडिशा उच्च न्यायालय ने उन याचिकाकर्ताओं से सहमति व्यक्त करते हुए, जिन्होंने पर्यावरणीय मंजूरी के बावजूद खदानों के सुस्त संचालन को उजागर किया था, कहा कि देरी के परिणामस्वरूप राज्य को औसतन 4,000 करोड़ रुपये का वार्षिक राजस्व नुकसान हुआ है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Environmental' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित। इसके Synonyms हैं: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural और Antonyms हैं: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic।

hinglishTracks.en: However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — हालाँकि, उद्योग के सूत्रों ने नाम न छापने की शर्त पर बोलते हुए, देरी के लिए मुख्य रूप से लंबी वन मंजूरी प्रक्रियाओं को जिम्मेदार ठहराया, जो अक्सर निर्धारित 18 महीने की समय सीमा से अधिक हो जाती है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — याचिकाकर्ता सिटीजन्स एक्शन फोरम (भुवनेश्वर) द्वारा उद्धृत आंकड़ों से पता चलता है कि वित्त वर्ष 2015 में 246 मिलियन टन प्रति वर्ष (एमटीपीए) खनन क्षमता को पर्यावरणीय मंजूरी दी गई थी, केवल 159 एमटीपीए का ही परिचालन किया गया था।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Environmental' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित। इसके Synonyms हैं: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural और Antonyms हैं: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic।

hinglishTracks.en: Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — अलग से, जून 2026 में खनन परामर्श कंपनी बिगमिंट द्वारा प्रकाशित आंकड़ों से पता चलता है कि ओडिशा ने वित्त वर्ष 26 में 278 एमटीपीए की पर्यावरणीय रूप से स्वीकृत क्षमता के मुकाबले 158 मीट्रिक टन लौह अयस्क का उत्पादन किया, जो लगभग 60% क्षमता उपयोग का संकेत देता है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Environmental' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित। इसके Synonyms हैं: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural और Antonyms हैं: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic।

hinglishTracks.en: The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, the highest-grade variety of iron ore.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — कम उपयोग की गई क्षमता विशेष रूप से महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि इसमें बड़े पैमाने पर हेमेटाइट शामिल है, जो लौह अयस्क की उच्चतम श्रेणी की किस्म है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Underutilisation' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: कम उपयोग — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Underutilisation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse और Antonyms हैं: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable।

hinglishTracks.en: The shortfall also raises questions over India’s continued dependence on imports.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — यह कमी भारत की आयात पर निरंतर निर्भरता पर भी सवाल उठाती है।।

hinglishTracks.en: According to the Mines Ministry, the country imported 12.3 MT of iron ore in FY26, incurring an expenditure of ₹11,115 crore.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — खान मंत्रालय के अनुसार, वित्त वर्ष 2026 में देश ने 12.3 मीट्रिक टन लौह अयस्क का आयात किया, जिस पर 11,115 करोड़ रुपये का खर्च आया।।

hinglishTracks.en: Odisha accounted for more than 50% of India’s domestic iron ore production during FY26.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — FY26 के दौरान भारत के घरेलू लौह अयस्क उत्पादन में ओडिशा का हिस्सा 50% से अधिक था।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Accountability' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता। इसके Synonyms हैं: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability और Antonyms हैं: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility।

hinglishTracks.en: Chhattisgarh contributed around 17.1%, followed by Karnataka at 16.6%.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — छत्तीसगढ़ ने लगभग 17.1% का योगदान दिया, उसके बाद कर्नाटक का 16.6% योगदान रहा।।

hinglishTracks.en: Capacity utilisation in the two states – albeit with significantly lower volumes than Odisha – stood at 62% and 80%, respectively, according to calculations based on BigMint data.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — बिगमिंट डेटा पर आधारित गणना के अनुसार, दोनों राज्यों में क्षमता उपयोग - हालांकि ओडिशा की तुलना में काफी कम मात्रा के साथ - क्रमशः 62% और 80% था।।

hinglishTracks.en: In January, the Odisha High Court directed that mining rights be mandatorily transferred to state-owned National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) to ensure “optimum utilisation of the mines” and “eradicate any burden on the government exchequer”.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — जनवरी में, ओडिशा उच्च न्यायालय ने निर्देश दिया कि "खदानों का इष्टतम उपयोग" सुनिश्चित करने और "सरकारी खजाने पर किसी भी बोझ को खत्म करने" के लिए खनन अधिकार अनिवार्य रूप से राज्य के स्वामित्व वाले राष्ट्रीय खनिज विकास निगम (एनएमडीसी) को हस्तांतरित किए जाएं।।

articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #14 of 30 (14 NOV)

📰 Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-producing states prompt concerns as India sets 2047 target

📌 Published: 14 Nov 2026, 09:35:55 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities. The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State. However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe. Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised. Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%. The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, the highest-grade variety of iron ore. The shortfall also raises questions over India’s continued dependence on imports. According to the Mines Ministry, the country imported 12.3 MT of iron ore in FY26, incurring an expenditure of ₹11,115 crore. Odisha accounted for more than 50% of India’s domestic iron ore production during FY26. Chhattisgarh contributed around 17.1%, followed by Karnataka at 16.6%. Capacity utilisation in the two states – albeit with significantly lower volumes than Odisha – stood at 62% and 80%, respectively, according to calculations based on BigMint data.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In January, the Odisha High Court directed that mining rights be mandatorily transferred to state-owned National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) to ensure “optimum utilisation of the mines” and “eradicate any burden on the government exchequer”.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Operationalisation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Operationalisation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Underutilisation (Adjective / Verb)
कम उपयोग — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Underutilisation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 📈 Economic, Banking & Finance passage on "Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-producing states prompt concerns as India sets 2047 target", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder,...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-pro' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-' should be permanently discontinued.

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities. The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State. However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe. Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised. Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%. The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, the highest-grade variety of iron ore. The shortfall also raises questions over India’s continued dependence on imports. According to the Mines Ministry, the country imported 12.3 MT of iron ore in FY26, incurring an expenditure of ₹11,115 crore. Odisha accounted for more than 50% of India’s domestic iron ore production during FY26. Chhattisgarh contributed around 17.1%, followed by Karnataka at 16.6%. Capacity utilisation in the two states – albeit with significantly lower volumes than Odisha – stood at 62% and 80%, respectively, according to calculations based on BigMint data.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In January, the Odisha High Court directed that mining rights be mandatorily transferred to state-owned National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) to ensure “optimum utilisation of the mines” and “eradicate any burden on the government exchequer”.

articles.title: Anthropic’s valuation can’t secure its moat
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Its engineers need to keep building progressively more capable models; the AI firm has also not established that it will be able to sustain its profitability after honouring its infra commitments

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic, best known as the maker of the Claude AI model, is preparing to go public at a valuation of $1.4 trillion, which could make the IPO one of the largest in history. However, this particular refrain has of late seemed more ominous than cause for optimism, and the Anthropic IPO could be no exception. The company has said it will offer 825 million shares at $70-78 apiece, to raise up to $64.4 billion. The valuation includes shares to be issued through employee options and other arrangements, and its market capitalisation based on outstanding shares is likely to be near $1 trillion. (It was valued at $965 billion in a private funding round in May.) Anthropic’s financial prospects depend on continuing to spend extraordinary sums of money. Its amended prospectus filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on November 10 revealed roughly $900 billion in spending commitments, almost entirely for computing infrastructure, until 2045. Of this, the company expects to incur half by 2030 and $70.7 billion in the twelve months from September 30. The filing also mentions another $150-175 billion in potential payments under arrangements sans fixed dollar commitments. Of this, the company expects to incur half by 2030 and $70.7 billion in the twelve months from September 30. The filing also mentions another $150-175 billion in potential payments under arrangements sans fixed dollar commitments. These figures clarify a colossal exposure to future demand that neither Anthropic nor other Big AI companies have thus far been able to guarantee. And while Anthropic’s revenue has also been growing, from $2.5 billion in the first three quarters of 2025 to $33.2 billion in the corresponding slice of 2026, the proposed fully diluted valuation exceeds annualised sales 17-fold. The current business model is, largely, to charge customers according to how many tokens they use to run their tasks on its AI models. From January to September 2026, this revenue constituted 79% of the total revenue, giving Anthropic a reason to encourage users to maximise token use, irrespective of changes in the value of the output generated — a tendency famously called tokenmaxxing. But three factors complicate this picture. First, Anthropic has said AI models released within the last six months accounted for more than 80% of its third quarter revenue, which means its engineers need to keep building progressively more capable models. Second, it has not established that it will be able to sustain its profitability after honouring its infrastructure commitments. The third factor is the most important, however: neither Anthropic nor its competitors, including OpenAI, currently has a lasting competitive advantage, a.k.a. a moat.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a recent study in the Journal of Economic Perspectives, researchers (including two affiliated with Amazon and Microsoft), reported that the price of AI inference of similar quality had fallen almost a thousandfold between late 2023 and late 2025, based on data from the OpenRouter marketplace. Given historical price rates, similar improvements would have taken computer storage two decades and lithium-ion batteries, five. The reasons include an explosion in the number of competing models, especially of the open-source variety, with customers being willing to pay less to use proprietary models as a result.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (14 NOV)

📰 Anthropic’s valuation can’t secure its moat

📌 Published: 14 Nov 2026, 11:51:19 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Its engineers need to keep building progressively more capable models; the AI firm has also not established that it will be able to sustain its profitability after honouring its infra commitments

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic, best known as the maker of the Claude AI model, is preparing to go public at a valuation of $1.4 trillion, which could make the IPO one of the largest in history. However, this particular refrain has of late seemed more ominous than cause for optimism, and the Anthropic IPO could be no exception. The company has said it will offer 825 million shares at $70-78 apiece, to raise up to $64.4 billion. The valuation includes shares to be issued through employee options and other arrangements, and its market capitalisation based on outstanding shares is likely to be near $1 trillion. (It was valued at $965 billion in a private funding round in May.) Anthropic’s financial prospects depend on continuing to spend extraordinary sums of money. Its amended prospectus filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on November 10 revealed roughly $900 billion in spending commitments, almost entirely for computing infrastructure, until 2045. Of this, the company expects to incur half by 2030 and $70.7 billion in the twelve months from September 30. The filing also mentions another $150-175 billion in potential payments under arrangements sans fixed dollar commitments. Of this, the company expects to incur half by 2030 and $70.7 billion in the twelve months from September 30. The filing also mentions another $150-175 billion in potential payments under arrangements sans fixed dollar commitments. These figures clarify a colossal exposure to future demand that neither Anthropic nor other Big AI companies have thus far been able to guarantee. And while Anthropic’s revenue has also been growing, from $2.5 billion in the first three quarters of 2025 to $33.2 billion in the corresponding slice of 2026, the proposed fully diluted valuation exceeds annualised sales 17-fold. The current business model is, largely, to charge customers according to how many tokens they use to run their tasks on its AI models. From January to September 2026, this revenue constituted 79% of the total revenue, giving Anthropic a reason to encourage users to maximise token use, irrespective of changes in the value of the output generated — a tendency famously called tokenmaxxing. But three factors complicate this picture. First, Anthropic has said AI models released within the last six months accounted for more than 80% of its third quarter revenue, which means its engineers need to keep building progressively more capable models. Second, it has not established that it will be able to sustain its profitability after honouring its infrastructure commitments. The third factor is the most important, however: neither Anthropic nor its competitors, including OpenAI, currently has a lasting competitive advantage, a.k.a. a moat.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a recent study in the Journal of Economic Perspectives, researchers (including two affiliated with Amazon and Microsoft), reported that the price of AI inference of similar quality had fallen almost a thousandfold between late 2023 and late 2025, based on data from the OpenRouter marketplace. Given historical price rates, similar improvements would have taken computer storage two decades and lithium-ion batteries, five. The reasons include an explosion in the number of competing models, especially of the open-source variety, with customers being willing to pay less to use proprietary models as a result.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Sustainability (Noun)
सतत विकास — पर्यावरण और भविष्य की पीढ़ियों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास।
✓ Syn: Viability, Eco-balance, Durability  |  ✖ Ant: Depletion, Unsustainability, Destruction
Capitalisation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Capitalisation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Anthropic’s valuation can’t secure its moat", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Its engineers need to keep building progressively more capable models; the AI firm has also not established that it will be able to sustain its...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Anthropic’s valuation can’t secure its moat' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Anthropic’s valuation can’t secure its moat' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Anthropic’s valuation can’t secure its moat' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Its engineers need to keep building progressively more capable models; the AI firm has also not established that it will be able to sustain its..." (Hinglish Arth: इसके इंजीनियरों को उत्तरोत्तर अधिक सक्षम मॉडल बनाते रहने की आवश्यकता है; एआई फर्म ने यह भी स्थापित नहीं किया है कि वह अपनी बुनियादी प्रतिबद्धताओं को पूरा करने के बाद अपनी लाभप्रदता को बनाए रखने में सक्षम होगी)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Anthropic’s valuation can’t secure its moat"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The reasons include an explosion in the number of competing models, especially of the open-source variety, with customers being willing to pay less...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The reasons include an explosion in the number of competing models, especially of the open-source variety, with customers being willing to pay less..." (Hinglish Arth: कारणों में प्रतिस्पर्धी मॉडलों की संख्या में विस्फोट शामिल है, विशेष रूप से ओपन-सोर्स किस्म के, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप ग्राहक मालिकाना मॉडल का उपयोग करने के लिए कम भुगतान करने को तैयार हैं।)

articles.title: Air pollution does not recognise State boundaries, coordinated action required: Union Minister
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav directed all agencies to move beyond planning and ensure rigorous, time-bound, and coordinated enforcement on the ground

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Saying that air pollution does not recognise State boundaries, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav on Saturday (November 14, 2026) emphasised the need for the coordinated implementation of pollution control measures across the National Capital Region (NCR), with real-time monitoring through Integrated Command and Control Centres (ICCCs) and direct accountability of field officers for violations. At a review meeting held to assess measures undertaken by Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan to mitigate air pollution in Delhi-NCR, he directed all agencies to move beyond planning and ensure rigorous, time-bound, and coordinated enforcement on the ground. The Minister directed State governments to nominate secretary-level officials for seven cities in Haryana, four cities in U.P., and four cities in Rajasthan to make them responsible for the implementation of pollution control measures through field visits and report to Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) on a weekly basis. The Minister directed all concerned States to install Automatic Number-plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras at fuel stations, integrated with VAHAN and Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) databases, for intensified action against old and polluting vehicles, failing which CAQM would initiate criminal prosecution against delinquent Transport Department officials after November 30. The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) was directed to immediately seal the identified 191 non-conforming polluting industries, which had not even placed orders for the installation of air pollution control devices (APCDs) despite repeated directions. Calling for strict implementation of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), Mr. Yadav called on NCR States to adopt Delhi’s hotspot-focused winter action plan, covering traffic management, work-from-home measures, construction restrictions and the prevention of open burning. Noting that only 3,221 km of the targeted 5,480 km of roads had been redeveloped, he directed road-owning agencies to prioritise pothole repairs, damaged footpaths, central verges, and end-to-end paving as per the CAQM framework, along with AI-based videographic surveys. For traffic decongestion, the Union Minister directed immediate action at the 233 identified congestion points across NCR, and fresh assessments by the respective States. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi was asked to complete the installation of multi-lane free flow systems at 154 Delhi border entry points by December 31.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Yadav said that real-time inputs from sensors, cameras, and satellites must be used alongside physical inspections to identify violations and ensure swift enforcement. “Coordinated efforts, field-level accountability, and visible action on the ground are essential to effectively address the challenge of air pollution in Delhi-NCR,” he said.

Calling for strict implementation of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), Mr. Yadav called on NCR States to adopt Delhi’s hotspot-focused winter action plan, covering traffic management, work-from-home measures, construction restrictions and the prevention of open burning. Noting that only 3,221 km of the targeted 5,480 km of roads had been redeveloped, he directed road-owning agencies to prioritise pothole repairs, damaged footpaths, central verges, and end-to-end paving as per the CAQM framework, along with AI-based videographic surveys. For traffic decongestion, the Union Minister directed immediate action at the 233 identified congestion points across NCR, and fresh assessments by the respective States. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi was asked to complete the installation of multi-lane free flow systems at 154 Delhi border entry points by December 31.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Yadav said that real-time inputs from sensors, cameras, and satellites must be used alongside physical inspections to identify violations and ensure swift enforcement. “Coordinated efforts, field-level accountability, and visible action on the ground are essential to effectively address the challenge of air pollution in Delhi-NCR,” he said.

hinglishTracks.en: Saying that air pollution does not recognise State boundaries, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav on Saturday (November 14, 2026) emphasised the need for the coordinated implementation of pollution control measures across the National Capital Region (NCR), with real-time monitoring through Integrated Command and Control Centres (ICCCs) and direct accountability of field officers for violations.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — यह कहते हुए कि वायु प्रदूषण राज्य की सीमाओं को नहीं पहचानता है, केंद्रीय पर्यावरण, वन और जलवायु परिवर्तन मंत्री भूपेन्द्र यादव ने शनिवार (14 नवंबर, 2026) को एकीकृत कमांड और नियंत्रण केंद्रों (आईसीसीसी) के माध्यम से वास्तविक समय की निगरानी और उल्लंघन के लिए फील्ड अधिकारियों की प्रत्यक्ष जवाबदेही के साथ राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र (एनसीआर) में प्रदूषण नियंत्रण उपायों के समन्वित कार्यान्वयन की आवश्यकता पर जोर दिया।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Environmental' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित। इसके Synonyms हैं: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural और Antonyms हैं: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic।

hinglishTracks.en: At a review meeting held to assess measures undertaken by Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan to mitigate air pollution in Delhi-NCR, he directed all agencies to move beyond planning and ensure rigorous, time-bound, and coordinated enforcement on the ground.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — दिल्ली-एनसीआर में वायु प्रदूषण को कम करने के लिए दिल्ली, हरियाणा, उत्तर प्रदेश और राजस्थान द्वारा किए गए उपायों का आकलन करने के लिए आयोजित एक समीक्षा बैठक में उन्होंने सभी एजेंसियों को योजना से आगे बढ़ने और जमीन पर कठोर, समयबद्ध और समन्वित कार्यान्वयन सुनिश्चित करने का निर्देश दिया।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Enforcement' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना। इसके Synonyms हैं: Implementation, Execution, Administration और Antonyms हैं: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver।

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (14 NOV)

📰 Air pollution does not recognise State boundaries, coordinated action required: Union Minister

📌 Published: 14 Nov 2026, 09:46:03 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav directed all agencies to move beyond planning and ensure rigorous, time-bound, and coordinated enforcement on the ground

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Saying that air pollution does not recognise State boundaries, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav on Saturday (November 14, 2026) emphasised the need for the coordinated implementation of pollution control measures across the National Capital Region (NCR), with real-time monitoring through Integrated Command and Control Centres (ICCCs) and direct accountability of field officers for violations. At a review meeting held to assess measures undertaken by Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan to mitigate air pollution in Delhi-NCR, he directed all agencies to move beyond planning and ensure rigorous, time-bound, and coordinated enforcement on the ground. The Minister directed State governments to nominate secretary-level officials for seven cities in Haryana, four cities in U.P., and four cities in Rajasthan to make them responsible for the implementation of pollution control measures through field visits and report to Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) on a weekly basis. The Minister directed all concerned States to install Automatic Number-plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras at fuel stations, integrated with VAHAN and Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) databases, for intensified action against old and polluting vehicles, failing which CAQM would initiate criminal prosecution against delinquent Transport Department officials after November 30. The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) was directed to immediately seal the identified 191 non-conforming polluting industries, which had not even placed orders for the installation of air pollution control devices (APCDs) despite repeated directions. Calling for strict implementation of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), Mr. Yadav called on NCR States to adopt Delhi’s hotspot-focused winter action plan, covering traffic management, work-from-home measures, construction restrictions and the prevention of open burning. Noting that only 3,221 km of the targeted 5,480 km of roads had been redeveloped, he directed road-owning agencies to prioritise pothole repairs, damaged footpaths, central verges, and end-to-end paving as per the CAQM framework, along with AI-based videographic surveys. For traffic decongestion, the Union Minister directed immediate action at the 233 identified congestion points across NCR, and fresh assessments by the respective States. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi was asked to complete the installation of multi-lane free flow systems at 154 Delhi border entry points by December 31.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Yadav said that real-time inputs from sensors, cameras, and satellites must be used alongside physical inspections to identify violations and ensure swift enforcement. “Coordinated efforts, field-level accountability, and visible action on the ground are essential to effectively address the challenge of air pollution in Delhi-NCR,” he said.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Enforcement (Noun)
सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना।
✓ Syn: Implementation, Execution, Administration  |  ✖ Ant: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Implementation (Noun)
क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।
✓ Syn: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment  |  ✖ Ant: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: As construction for hyperscale Google AI data centres go full throttle in Visakhapatnam, farmers say promised land and jobs have not arrived

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The muddy, unpaved road into Tarluvada runs along a wall of tall blue corrugated iron sheets. Once, it was just farms and forests. What is being built behind the wall is hidden from view. Just beyond, on the hill locals call Chukka Konda, a broad swathe of the slope has been stripped back to red earth and cut into terraces, stark against the green around it. Last year, when government officials came to the small village in Anandapuram mandal on the outskirts of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, they had made big promises: plentiful jobs and opportunities once Google, the American tech corporation, built its hyperscale 1 GW AI data centre there. Today, the village is uneasy. Many farmers refuse to talk. Leaders of Left parties say they are not allowed to meet the locals to understand their problems, and those who speak to them are being targeted and harassed by the police.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Sunday Magazine / Artificial Intelligence / Visakhapatnam / technology (general) / data management storage / water / environmental pollution / power (infrastructure) / water pollution / air pollution

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (14 NOV)

📰 Age of AI: behind Tarluvada’s blue wall in Visakhapatnam

📌 Published: 14 Nov 2026, 06:25:04 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: As construction for hyperscale Google AI data centres go full throttle in Visakhapatnam, farmers say promised land and jobs have not arrived

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The muddy, unpaved road into Tarluvada runs along a wall of tall blue corrugated iron sheets. Once, it was just farms and forests. What is being built behind the wall is hidden from view. Just beyond, on the hill locals call Chukka Konda, a broad swathe of the slope has been stripped back to red earth and cut into terraces, stark against the green around it. Last year, when government officials came to the small village in Anandapuram mandal on the outskirts of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, they had made big promises: plentiful jobs and opportunities once Google, the American tech corporation, built its hyperscale 1 GW AI data centre there. Today, the village is uneasy. Many farmers refuse to talk. Leaders of Left parties say they are not allowed to meet the locals to understand their problems, and those who speak to them are being targeted and harassed by the police.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Sunday Magazine / Artificial Intelligence / Visakhapatnam / technology (general) / data management storage / water / environmental pollution / power (infrastructure) / water pollution / air pollution
